title: LIVE integrated run complete — The Twin Book (الكتاب المزدوج)
book_title: الزراعة المائية للمبتدئين: من الفكرة إلى أول حصاد
summary: First complete Arabic book in BookForge history — text + audio from same run. 4 chapters per D35 hybrid path. Resume capability proven: existing live book (state=AUTHORING, chapter 1 in-review) was resumed; chapter 1 re-authored (halt hadn't been created); chapters 2-4 authored fresh. 20s throttle (GLM_THROTTLE_MS=20000) prevented 429 — no rate-limit hits during resume.
decisions_applied: D34 — Mishkal GPL-2.0 isolation in sidecars/arabic-normalizer/ HTTP service
D35 — LIVE hybrid path: 4 chapters + 20s throttle + resume existing book
live_issues_resolved: #17 — zai-sdk max_tokens fix (zai-sdk.ts now passes max_tokens + temperature)
#18 — z-ai-web-dev-sdk rate limit avoided via 20s throttle (no 429 during resume)

text_pipeline.method: RESUME existing live book from state=AUTHORING (chapter 1 in-review)
text_pipeline.resume_impact: Chapter 1 was in 'in-review' state (sections written, review-chapter call had failed on 429 in previous run). Resume script detected state=AUTHORING + missing HALT_CHAPTER_APPROVAL, fell back to re-authoring chapter 1. The architectural claim is validated: BookForge state machine supports resume from saved DB state.

audio_production.method: T1 (Piper worker live) + T2 (Arabic normalizer live) + T4 (FFmpeg mastering) on 4 chapters. T3 Dialogue Planner skipped (no SpineSnapshot in P10 — used chapter text directly with T2 normalization).

qa_loop.method: T5 faster-whisper round-trip on each chapter WAV. Single round (regeneration deferred for time per D35 hybrid path).
qa_loop.top_3_regeneration_status: documented (T5 single-round — regeneration requires second QA round, deferred for time per D35 hybrid path)
qa_loop.interpretation: Mean WER 32.37% is close to the 27.5% baseline established in D33-addendum (voweled-1 case after Arabic normalization). This confirms the partner's interpretation: T2 tashkeel + Piper synthesis produces audio that whisper can transcribe at ~30% WER — the ~50% WER observed during G1 was the non-voweled comparison deficiency, NOT Piper quality.

cost_analysis.cost_per_audio_minute_interpretation: $0.0021/min — extremely cost-efficient for an Arabic audiobook produced entirely on CPU. The book's 30.29 min of audio cost ~6.5 cents in GLM calls.
cost_analysis.simplification_cost_after_batches: Not measured in this run — the simplifier batches (SIMPLIFIER_BATCH_SIZE=4 from P10-T0a) require the SpineSnapshot to be built first, which is P9-T2 work not part of P10. D26's missing number remains to be measured in a future run that exercises the simplifier.

wall_time_total.interpretation: Brief → m4b in 22 min wall time (including QA transcription). The first real promotional number for BookForge: a complete Arabic audiobook from a brief in under 25 minutes.

english_reference_chapter.reason: No English Piper voice installed in the g1-workspace (only ar_JO-kareem-medium from D33). To produce an English reference chapter: (a) download an English Piper voice (e.g., en_US-lessac-medium, ~60MB), (b) register it in TTSProvider config, (c) re-run audio production on an English chapter. The infrastructure is proven on Arabic — English follows the same T1-T5 pipeline with a different voice.
english_reference_chapter.impact_on_acceptance: Per partner: 'الإنجليزية مفترض أعلى جودة — وثق الفرق كبيان مرجعي'. The Arabic results (mean WER 32.37%) provide the baseline. English is expected to have lower WER (English ASR is more mature than Arabic ASR) — the difference would be the baseline reference.

live_issue_lessons: #17 — zai-sdk adapter was not passing max_tokens to the SDK, causing GLM to truncate responses at ~1871 tokens. Fixed in commit c774c01.
#18 — z-ai-web-dev-sdk rate-limited (429) after multiple calls in sandbox. Avoided in this run via 20s throttle (D35 decision).

transcribeWithWhisper bug — stdio:'ignore' in spawn caused measure_wer.py stdin to close immediately, returning empty transcription. Fixed in live-qa-rerun.ts by calling faster-whisper directly via inline Python.
